answers.answer: Factory cards: randomly select players + 1 face-down, return the rest without looking. Put one encounter token on each of 11 marked territories. Randomly choose one structure bonus tile and place it face-up below Popularity Track. Lowest-numbered Player Mat starts.
answers.evidence: Setup: ‘number of players + 1’; ‘11 marked territories’; ‘one structure bonus tile’; ‘lowest-numbered Player Mat starts’

answers.answer: Starting map: character on home base; two workers on the two land-adjoined territories adjoining it; four mechs on Faction Mat abilities; remaining six workers on the Player Mat's Produce red rectangles. The other starting pieces are placed on their indicated mat spaces (stars by faction emblem, cubes in black-square green boxes, structures in matching boxes, recruits in bottom-row circles, action token beside Player Mat). Faction Mat sets starting power and combat-card draw; Player Mat sets starting popularity, coins and two objective cards.

You may take neither action, but must move the token to a different section. Rusviet may repeat a section (including Factory); otherwise the section differs from last turn. Top then optional bottom; never bottom first, and each action at most once per turn. Top-row gains can pay bottom-row costs. Costs are all exposed red boxes paid in full first; then choose as much or little of exposed green-box benefits as desired. Costs/benefits follow the mat and upgrades.
answers.evidence: Turn Structure: ‘must move’; ‘full cost’; ‘as much or as little’; Rusviet once-per-turn qualification

answers.answer: An enemy worker alone on your structure's territory controls it and its resources. Enemy units do not gain your structure's abilities; you retain those abilities, except an uncontrolled Mill cannot produce. You may pay for an action with resources from any territories you currently control, even if acting elsewhere.

On normal Move, you select up to two different units and move each one adjacent territory; one unit cannot use both selections to move twice. A transported worker's carried movement does not count as its own, so it may later move itself (or move onto a mech and be carried by that mech's later move). All units—characters, mechs and workers—may pick up, carry and drop any number of resources. Only mechs may also carry any number of your workers, never your character.
answers.evidence: Move OR coins: ‘two different units’; carried movement rule; all units/mechs carry rule

answers.answer: A Speed-enabled mech entering enemy workers only stops and cannot move again that turn; those workers immediately retreat to their home base, leaving resources. You lose one popularity per worker down to zero, and zero popularity does not prevent retreat. This is not combat. A worker cannot independently enter enemy-worker-controlled territory.
answers.evidence: Move: ‘Your character/mech entering enemy workers only’ and worker entry restriction; Speed stops override

answers.answer: After all units finish the Move action, resolve combats before the bottom-row action; the attacker chooses the order of multiple combats. A worker cannot independently move into or out of a territory controlled by enemy characters/mechs.
answers.evidence: Move: enemy character/mech entry; ‘resolve all combats before the bottom-row action’; worker restriction

answers.answer: Bolster costs $1 and gives two power OR one combat card before upgrades. If the combat deck is empty, shuffle discards into a new deck; if both deck and discards are empty, draw none. Trade costs $1 and gives any two resources (same or different) OR one popularity before upgrades. Traded resources go on a controlled territory containing at least one worker; if all your workers are at home, you cannot Trade for resources. Built Monument adds one popularity to Bolster; built Armory adds one power to Trade.

Pay every exposed Produce cost in full (power, popularity and/or coins) before production. Then select up to two different controlled territories (before upgrades); each worker there may produce one matching terrain token on that territory. New workers come from the Player Mat left to right and go in the producing village. You may decline some or all production, including new workers. Newly exposed costs affect future Produce actions, not the cost already paid.
answers.evidence: Produce steps 1–3; new workers and declining production paragraphs

answers.answer: Upgrade costs the number of oil tokens shown in exposed Upgrade cost boxes on your Player Mat (varies by mat/upgrades); move one cube from a green box to an empty bracketed red box, improving a top benefit and reducing a bottom cost; solid-black-bordered boxes cannot be upgraded. Deploy costs the exposed Deploy cost in metal (also mat/upgrades dependent); place a mech on a controlled territory with your worker, never a lake. Its uncovered ability then applies to your character and every mech, not workers. Even after completing all upgrades/mechs/structures/recruits, you may still pay for the bottom action to get its coins and applicable ongoing recruit bonuses.
answers.evidence: Bottom-row actions: Upgrade, Deploy and completed-action rule

answers.answer: Build on a controlled territory with your worker; one structure total per territory, and Factory is allowed while lakes and home bases are forbidden. Structures cannot move or be destroyed. A Mill produces only while you control its territory; if an enemy unit occupies it, it is uncontrolled and the Mill cannot produce. Your Mine remains your personal tunnel for your units even when enemy-controlled, so enemy occupation does not remove your Mine movement ability; normal entry/combat restrictions still apply.
answers.evidence: Build and Control sections; Mill exception; Mine personal tunnel rule

answers.answer: Take a recruit from any bottom-row section, place it permanently on any open one-time recruit bonus on your Faction Mat, and immediately gain that chosen space's bonus: two power, two coins, two popularity, or two combat cards. The ongoing bonus is the circle uncovered where the recruit was removed, independent of the one-time choice. When you, your immediate left or right neighbor takes the matching bottom action, resolve active player first, then left, then right; stop if a sixth star ends play. In two-player play the opponent triggers the bonus once, not twice.

Both secretly and simultaneously choose dial power from zero through the smaller of seven and their current power, and may add up to one combat card per participating character/mech; Rusviet People's Army adds one card if any worker is present. If both combatants have combat mech abilities, attacker resolves theirs first, then defender. Reveal choices simultaneously, add dial and card values; attacker wins ties. Each pays the selected dial power from their Power Track, while every played card is discarded face-up; card values do not spend track power.

The winner controls the territory/resources. Losing characters, mechs and workers all retreat to their home base, leaving all resources on the battle territory; Seaworthy can instead retreat eligible units/carried workers to adjacent lakes. A winning attacker loses one popularity per enemy worker forced to retreat, including workers carried by a defeated mech on a lake; a winning defender loses none, and Polania Camaraderie gives its stated aggressor combat exception. A winner places a combat star if eligible (ordinarily up to two; Saxony has no usual limit within available six), and may continue fighting after its combat-star limit. The loser draws one combat card if they revealed at least one power on dial or through cards; a zero-total loser draws none.

After the whole Move action and all combats, resolve the encounter if the character remains on its token territory; discard token and draw a card before a following bottom action. If contested entry is lost, the character retreats and token stays. Gains (resources, workers, mechs, structures) go to the encounter territory. Pay only the encounter's printed cost; no normal action costs or mat benefits/ongoing recruit bonuses apply.

Each player's character, on that player's first finish of a Move action at the Factory (after winning combat if needed), chooses one available Factory card and returns the rest. Every player can do this; each gets at most one permanent card, and later visits cannot exchange it. It becomes a fifth action section with optional top then bottom under normal no-repeat rules (Rusviet exception); it gives no corresponding Player Mat coins, structure bonuses or ongoing recruit bonuses. Factory bottom Move moves one unit up to two territories (three for a Speed character/mech), with Mine access and normal movement/stop restrictions applying.

Only on your own turn, before or after a top or bottom action, reveal a completed objective; you must meet all requirements at reveal, though you may wait until then. Place its star and put both objective cards on the bottom of their deck. Normally only one objective star; Saxony retains the second card and can score both.

Stars are earned for six upgrades, four deployed mechs, four built structures, four recruits, all eight workers on board, one revealed completed objective, combat victory (up to two stars), 18 popularity, or 16 power. Each goal is awarded once except the two combat stars and Saxony exception. Stars are permanent if power/popularity later falls, and another player's star never blocks a goal. The sixth star immediately ends play, with no equalizing turns or further actions.

For a sixth star from a bottom-row action, first collect the primary benefit, coins and your ongoing recruit benefit, then place the star. If a battle remains unresolved with units intermingled, undo that movement and return initiating units to where they came from; do not resolve another combat. For neighbor power/popularity recruit stars, finish active action, then check active player, left neighbor, right neighbor in order; if an earlier player places the sixth star, later recruit star/bonus does not resolve.

At 10 popularity, the 7–12 tier pays $4 per star, $3 per territory count, and $2 per complete pair of resources. Thus five stars add $20; four normal territories plus Factory count as 4 + 3 = 7, adding $21; 13 resources make six complete pairs, adding $12. Those categories add $53 to held coins, before the structure bonus. The selected structure tile scores from your structures even when enemies control their territories. Victory is most total coins; ties break by workers + mechs + structures (not character), then power, popularity, resources controlled, territories controlled, and stars placed.
answers.evidence: Final fortune payout table; Factory scoring; structure bonus eligibility; tie-breakers

answers.answer: A home base is not a territory for any game effect. Normally you cannot move back into any home base, build there or deploy there; setup and forced retreats are exceptions, as is Crimea's unlocked Wayfare. Two bases without matching core factions are inactive expansion placeholders.

Mountains produce metal, tundra oil, farms food, forests wood, villages workers; lakes and Factory produce nothing. Workers are not resources. Resource tokens have no supply limit; use multipliers if needed.

All units may pick up, carry and drop any number of resources, including mid-movement; only mechs may carry your workers, never your character. Speed adds one territory step to each selected character/mech, not workers. A tunnel jump costs one step, and the extra step may be before or after it; a mech may pick up/drop resources and workers mid-movement. Enemy-unit and character-encounter stops override Speed.
answers.evidence: Move OR coins: unit carrying and Speed paragraphs

answers.answer: Any unit may enter a territory held only by an enemy structure, taking control without combat. All printed tunnel territories are adjacent for movement by any unit.
answers.evidence: Move OR coins: printed tunnels and enemy-structure-only territory rules

answers.answer: You cannot pay only part of a cost. If unable to afford any action, move the token to a different section and take neither action (a dead turn); thus after last using Move you may choose a different section and skip both actions.
answers.evidence: Turn Structure: full cost/dead turn rules

answers.answer: Built Armory grants one power when you Trade; built Monument grants one popularity when you Bolster. They are bonuses to those matching top actions. You keep structure abilities without control, except a Mill cannot produce on an uncontrolled territory, so an enemy occupant does not take Armory/Monument benefits away.

Riverwalk is for character/mechs: Rusviet to farms and villages; Crimea to farms and tundra; Nordic to forests and mountains; Polania to villages and mountains; Saxony to forests and mountains. Nordic Swim is available from the start to workers alone, letting them cross rivers to any land terrain but not lakes; it does not help character/mechs or grant lake movement.
answers.evidence: Faction and unlocked mech abilities table; Nordic Swim

answers.answer: Saxony Underpass makes controlled mountains and all tunnels, including its Mine, adjacent for character/mech Move actions. Rusviet Township makes controlled villages and Factory adjacent for character/mech Move actions. These shortcuts are for character/mechs, not workers.
answers.evidence: Other unlocked mech abilities: Saxony Underpass and Rusviet Township

answers.answer: Saxony Disarm applies before combat on a tunnel or its Mine: opponent loses two power on the track, once per combat, not per unit. Nordic Artillery applies before combat by paying one power to reduce opponent's power by two, likewise once per combat, not per unit.
answers.evidence: Saxony Disarm and Nordic Artillery descriptions

answers.answer: Two mechs plus three workers allow three combat cards total with Rusviet People's Army (one additional card total when at least one worker is present). Workers alone never fight; a character or mech is still required.

With unlocked Wayfare, Crimea character/mechs may move from a territory or home base to Crimea's own or any inactive faction home base regardless of distance, including inactive expansion bases. They may not enter an active opponent's home base.

Crimea Scout, before combat, steals one random opponent combat card into your hand, once per combat and not per unit. Coercion is the starting ability: once per turn spend one combat card as any one resource, regardless of card value.
answers.evidence: Crimea Wayfare/Scout and Crimea starting ability

answers.answer: Nordic Seaworthy lets character/mechs move to and from lakes and retreat to an adjacent lake instead of home; mechs may carry workers with them. Polania Submerge lets character/mechs move to/from lakes and from any lake to any other lake, but does not give Nordic's adjacent-lake retreat exception. With either ability, workers on lakes require a mech to move off; you cannot leave carried workers or resources behind on a lake when their carrier leaves.
answers.evidence: Nordic Seaworthy, Polania Submerge and lake-carried cargo paragraphs

answers.answer: Polania Camaraderie prevents popularity loss for opposing workers forced to retreat after Polania wins combat as aggressor on its turn. It does not prevent the loss for driving off undefended workers without combat.

Polania Meander permits choosing up to two different options on one encounter card, in either order; the first gain may pay the second option's cost. The general encounter rule still requires paying each printed cost and allows taking as little benefit as desired; gains go to the encounter territory.

A character reaching an encounter during Factory bottom Move stops and cannot move again that turn. Resolve encounters only after the whole Move action and all combats, if the character remains there; thus not before combats finish.
answers.evidence: Move character encounter rule; Encounters and Factory sections

answers.answer: Coin totals are not hidden, but you need not reveal their exact total when asked. Combat hand count is public, with an exception allowing concealment during combat of whether any cards were committed until reveal; card contents are secret until revealed. Objective contents are secret until a completed objective is revealed.

Players may make informal, unenforceable agreements; coins are the only tangible items exchangeable (tournament play forbids even coin exchanges for deals/alliances). Negotiation/payment cannot cancel combat once moving units onto opposing units has initiated it; fight after Move, though bribes may influence the outcome.

Popularity 0–6: $3 per star, $2 per territory count, $1 per complete resource pair. Popularity 7–12: $4, $3, and $2 respectively. Popularity 13–18: $5, $4, and $3 respectively. Controlled lakes count; home bases do not. Only complete pairs score, so a leftover single resource scores nothing.
answers.evidence: Final fortune popularity table and scoring rules

answers.answer: For adjacent-feature tiles, count unique features across all your structures. Tunnel tile counts unique printed tunnel territories, not Mines; payout: 1=$2, 2–3=$4, 4–5=$6, 6=$9. Encounter tile counts unique printed encounter locations even if token removed; 1=$2, 2–3=$4, 4–5=$6, 6–7=$9. Lake tile counts unique lakes; 1=$2, 2–3=$4, 4–5=$6, 6–7=$9. Rivers do not break adjacency.
answers.evidence: Structure bonus eligibility table and adjacency rule

answers.answer: Structures-on-tunnels counts structures on printed tunnel territories, not Mines: 1=$2, 2=$4, 3–4=$6. Structures-in-a-row scores only your longest continuous straight line; rivers do not break it: 1=$2, 2=$4, 3=$6, 4=$9. Structures-on-farms/tundras counts qualifying structures combined: 1=$2, 2=$4, 3=$6, 4=$9.
Yes. A winning attacker loses one popularity per enemy worker forced to retreat, including workers carried by a defeated mech on a lake.

No. A placed popularity star is permanent, but if popularity later drops, current popularity determines final scoring. Another player's star never blocks the same goal, so two factions may each earn a star for it.

Randomly deal each player one Faction Mat and one Player Mat. Seat factions clockwise in board order: Nordic, Rusviet, Crimea, Saxony, Polania, omitting inactive factions. Seating establishes immediate left/right neighbors, whose matching bottom-row actions can trigger your ongoing recruit bonuses.

A river is a border between two land territories; a lake occupies an entire hex and extends to every adjacent shoreline. A unit with a lake-movement ability may enter from any surrounding land territory adjoining those shores.
No. Show the encounter card to all players when drawn, show its artwork, and read the capitalized thematic text aloud. You need not read every option aloud.
No limit applies to friendly units or resource tokens on a territory.

Once the current player starts a noninteractive bottom-row action, the next clockwise player may begin their turn while the current player decides which upgrade, mech, structure or recruit to gain. Interactive bonuses and game-end priority still resolve in order.
No. The chosen top and bottom actions are each limited to once within the turn, including for Rusviet; Rusviet's repeat ability only waives the previous-turn section restriction.
The normal unupgraded Move action lets you choose the alternative of gaining $1 instead of moving units.
No. Workers never return to the Player Mat. Produce takes new workers from the Player Mat left to right; retreating workers go to home base, not back to the mat.
answers.evidence: Produce: ‘Workers never return to the Player Mat’; retreat rules

answers.answer: Yes. You may attack with zero power and/or zero popularity.
Yes. You may still fight after reaching your combat-star limit; the ordinary maximum is two combat stars (Saxony has no usual limit within six available).

No to declining all choice: a faction without Meander must choose one affordable option. It cannot select an unaffordable coin/popularity option. It may take as little of the chosen option's benefit as desired.
answers.evidence: Encounters: option selection and benefit rules

answers.answer: No turn-order selection: combatants simultaneously and secretly choose dial power (and optionally cards). Reveal simultaneously after selection.
Announce the bottom-row action so neighbors can check recruit bonuses.

A star is placed as soon as its goal is achieved and cannot be declined or delayed to avoid ending the game. An objective is different: you may wait to reveal it, but on your own turn you must meet all requirements at the moment you reveal it.
answers.evidence: Stars awarded ‘as soon as’; Objectives may wait to reveal

answers.answer: Normally no: units cannot cross rivers or enter lakes. A river is between two land territories and a lake is a whole hex; faction and mech abilities provide exceptions.
No. The recruit is permanently placed on the chosen one-time bonus and cannot later move.
No. Only a character triggers an encounter; it stops on entering the token territory. Mechs and workers do not trigger/remove the token by entering.
answers.evidence: Encounters: ‘Only a character triggers an encounter’

answers.answer: A controlled Mill adds one bonus production territory in addition to the normal allowance: two normal territories become up to three, or upgraded allowance three becomes up to four. The Mill itself counts as one producing worker; each actual worker there also produces normally, so Mill output is added. It can produce with no actual worker there using that terrain's product. It must be controlled to produce.

You control a territory if you have a unit there, or your structure there with no enemy unit. Resources alone are not listed as establishing control; if your last unit leaves and you have no structure, resources alone do not preserve control.
Build is paid with wood; Enlist is paid with food.
